headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors when AutoGen’s code-executing workflows feed Notion AI’s workspace-backed outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and execute shell commands, while Notion AI ingests workspace pages and team knowledge base content. If AutoGen outputs are copied into Notion or shared via workspace files, prompt-like content can influence Notion’s RAG-style responses. The pathway is plausible but not default and lacks a documented direct bridge.
conditions: IF AutoGen outputs are pasted into Notion pages that Notion AI later summarizes
IF a shared workspace file is used as an instruction channel between the agents
mitigations: Keep agent outputs in separate folders/pages
Add a human review step before copying AutoGen text into Notion
Use explicit delimiters for quoted content
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted pages into Notion AI workflows

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen can read the filesystem and has broad network egress; Notion AI can access workspace pages and databases under the user’s Notion permissions. If sensitive application data is placed in shared workspace content or files, both agents can expose it through their respective backends. The shared-data pathway is credible, though not proven by a documented direct integration.
conditions: IF sensitive application data is stored in files AutoGen can read and then copied into Notion pages
IF Notion workspace pages contain secrets or regulated data that Notion AI can access
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared workspaces
Restrict Notion pages to non-sensitive summaries
Use separate workspaces for agent inputs and outputs
Redact sensitive fields before either agent processes them

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has filesystem write capability and can spawn subprocesses; Notion AI has shared workspace state across members and can modify workspace content within user permissions. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace artifacts, concurrent edits can overwrite or desynchronize content. The conflict is plausible in default collaborative setups, though Notion lacks host-level write access.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same shared document or exported file
IF AutoGen writes artifacts that are later imported into the same Notion workspace page
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Use one-way export from AutoGen into Notion
Lock shared files during edits
Version outputs with timestamps before import

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code, plans, or facts from tool use, and Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content. If Notion treats AutoGen-produced text as authoritative, errors can propagate into summaries or decisions. This is a realistic default workflow risk, but there is no evidence of autonomous downstream action beyond workspace content.
conditions: IF Notion AI is asked to summarize or answer from AutoGen-generated pages without verification
IF AutoGen-generated claims are reused as source material for downstream workspace decisions
mitigations: Mark AutoGen outputs as unverified
Require source links for factual claims
Add a verification checklist before publishing summaries
Separate draft and approved pages

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen can handle model provider API keys and broad filesystem data, while Notion AI accesses workspace pages under the invoking user’s Notion permissions and sends content to vendor backends. If regulated data such as EU PII or confidential business records is placed in Notion and then processed by AutoGen or Notion AI, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Notion pages processed by Notion AI
IF AutoGen is configured to send the same data to external model providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Use a DPA-approved workspace only
Minimize retention by deleting drafts promptly
Review vendor data-processing terms before use
